_comment: Live config. Both Gemini Pro-tier options are dead ends: gemini-3.1-pro-preview hit a hard 429 quota-exceeded (needs billing enabled, not just a low free allowance) and gemini-2.5-pro came back 404 'no longer available to new users' - a real decommission, not a rate issue. A role's value can be a single {provider, model, ...} dict, or a LIST of them - a fallback chain tried in preference order, falling back only once a candidate's own internal retries are fully exhausted (see providers.call_model/_dispatch). 2026-09-20, several changes the same night, in order: (1) swapped action/character/atmosphere/unify off gemini-3.6-flash onto gemini-3.5-flash-lite, moved editor the other way (3.5-flash-lite -> 3.6-flash), after three straight days of 503 'high demand' storms outlasting the full retry backoff - the run that nailed it down failed on action, the very FIRST call of a fresh regeneration, proving it's the model under sustained load, not any one pass's payload. (2) Every role turned into an explicit fallback chain, at the user's direct request to hedge against a whole provider having a bad night. (3) run_chapter.py caps how many fresh prose passes ONE run attempts (MAX_NEW_PASSES_PER_RUN, default 2) before stopping cleanly (exit 0) and leaving the rest for the next scheduled fire. (4) Groq REMOVED from action/character/atmosphere/unify/editor's chains - live proof it can't serve them: editor's Gemini candidate genuinely exhausted its quota (a real 429, not a demand spike), the chain correctly fell back to Groq's openai/gpt-oss-120b, and THAT immediately hit a 413 'tokens per minute (TPM): Limit 8000, Requested 11990' - the exact same 8000 TPM ceiling that killed the smaller gpt-oss-20b weeks earlier. The cap is evidently on the account/tier, not the model size, so a bigger Groq model was never going to help once canon.md + the motif ledger + a full prompt push a request past ~8000 tokens, which every one of these five roles' payloads now routinely does. Groq stays on skeleton and summariser ONLY, where the payload is provably small (skeleton never includes the motif section; summariser never sends canon.md at all) - both have run on Groq without a single TPM failure across the whole project. The five heavy roles now chain straight from Gemini to Mistral/Cerebras, both genuinely different infrastructure and, as of this change, still completely untested live - worth verifying they actually work before trusting them further. Mistral and Cerebras were both parked earlier in the project for their own reasons (Mistral: 429 rate_limited on the very first call, two different roles, two separate runs; Cerebras: the specific model tried then, llama-4-maverick-17b-128e-instruct, was archived) - as a fallback tier they cost nothing to re-list regardless. Picked mistral-small-latest deliberately (a '-latest' alias, not a dated snapshot) to dodge the exact version-churn that broke qwen3.6-27b and gemini-3.1-pro-preview elsewhere in this file; Cerebras's llama3.3-70b was picked as a different, currently-supported model from the archived one - it wasn't: the very next live run (editor, after Gemini's real daily-quota 429 and Mistral's real rate-limit 429 both correctly exhausted in the chain) hit a genuine 404 'model_not_found' on it too, crashing the run outright since it was the last candidate with nowhere left to fall back to (and discarding that run's already-checkpointed action/character passes along with it, per the existing discard-on-crash cleanup). Cerebras had deprecated llama-3.3-70b account-wide by this point - corroborated externally (a docs PR removing it as 'no longer offered in the Dashboard', and another integration's own live /v1/models listing for its Cerebras key returning only gpt-oss-120b/a gemma variant/a qwen variant, no Llama at all). Swapped Cerebras's model to gpt-oss-120b - its own hosted copy, a different endpoint from Groq's identically-named model, so no shared TPM/quota. Not yet verified live for heavy payloads (unify, editor) - if it hits its own version of a rate/TPM wall there, that's a new, separate finding, not this one repeating. summariser also carries reasoning_effort/reasoning_format on its Groq candidate - its original model (qwen/qwen3.6-27b) was a reasoning model that emitted <think>...</think> as literal text sharing the same token budget as the real answer, burning through its budget without ever finishing its reasoning, let alone writing the summary. These fields (read by providers._openai_compatible, ignored by candidates that don't set them) disable reasoning outright and strip it from the response as a second line of defense. qwen/qwen3.6-27b itself was then decommissioned outright (404 model_not_found) - moved summariser's primary to openai/gpt-oss-20b, the smaller sibling of skeleton's gpt-oss-120b: same family, distinct model ID so no shared TPM concerns, small enough for a task that never sends canon.md anyway. Two live 400s fixing that: qwen accepted reasoning_effort 'none' but gpt-oss only accepts low/medium/high (set to 'low'), and reasoning_format isn't supported by gpt-oss at all - had to drop it. Not a problem in practice: gpt-oss puts reasoning in its own response field rather than qwen's literal inline tags, so the content field _openai_compatible() reads was never going to carry reasoning text regardless. _strip_thinking() in passes.py stays as a no-cost safety net for whatever model ends up on this role next. IMPORTANT: never push a new commit to main while a draft.yml run is in progress - its own end-of-run checkpoint commit/push can get rejected as a non-fast-forward conflict, silently losing that run's work (caught live doing exactly this).
